question.worked_solution:
Expanding the binomial and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(1+\frac{1}{x})}^{2}\text{d}x & =\int (1+\frac{2}{x}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{{x}^{-2+1}}{-2+1}+C \\  & =x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-\frac{1}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, let's rewrite the constant so that we can combine it with the natural logarithm. For any constant $C,$ we can always write $C=2\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ where $K$ is some other positive constant. Doing this allows us to combine the constant with $2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|$ term, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(1+\frac{1}{x})}^{2}\text{d}x & =x-\frac{1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =x-\frac{1}{x}+2(\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =x-\frac{1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|x|).\end{aligned}
$$
